title: Measure flexible-drive resonance with Bode analysis
physicalPurpose: Measure frequency-dependent shaft response and compare loop-shaping candidates without applying unqualified gains.
principalTechnique: Measured Bode response and stability margins
objective: Measure the flexible-drive frequency response, expose resonance, and compare qualified unshaped and resonance-shaped margins.

simplifications: Fixed inertia, stiffness, and viscous damping
Ideal torque actuation inside declared limits
No backlash, higher shaft modes, drive dynamics, or protection model

baseline.limitation: The unshaped loop has a large resonant peak and approximately 6.9 degrees phase margin.

change.decision: Accept for further simulation only when measured response, all crossings, margins, and perturbed-model checks meet the declared criteria.

acceptance.window: 60 through 120 seconds after the transient-discard interval
qualified analytical sweep across every retained gain crossover
qualified analytical sweep across every retained gain crossover

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Requested and applied torque differ unexpectedly or applied torque reaches a limit
Actual sample timing or plant identity differs from the reviewed experiment
safety.restorationMode: Disable the experiment, command zero torque, and restart all three simulated drives from the 1000-rpm operating point
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised drive engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No candidate gain is applied by this lesson
Simulation evidence cannot authorise excitation or controller changes on a physical flexible drive
Physical work requires independent mechanical resonance, topology, protection, operating-envelope, abort, rollback, and immediate approval review

video.viewerOutcome: Measure a flexible-drive frequency response, recognize resonance, and reject a loop-shaping candidate when its margins or model robustness are inadequate.

learning.context: Three equivalent simulated flexible drives receive equal torque amplitudes at low, resonant, and high frequencies.
learning.reason: Root locus and one transient do not directly expose frequency-dependent resonance, phase loss, or full-loop margins.
theory: Sinusoidal steady-state amplitude and timing define magnitude and phase.
Bode plots place magnitude and phase against logarithmic frequency.
Every qualified crossover contributes to gain, phase, and delay-margin decisions.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate the three plant responses and the unshaped and shaped gain crossovers and phase margins before enabling a probe.
practicalPreparation: Verify plant identity, operating point, units, quality, timing, limits, seed, restoration, and Simulation evidence.
Declare the transient-discard and fitting windows, tolerances, aborts, and candidate rules before testing.
learning.baseline: Measure the lightly damped plant and calculate the unshaped gain-five loop's resonant peak and small phase margin.
learning.change: Calculate an unapplied resonance-shaped candidate with the same controller gain and test its model dependence.
learning.comparison: Change only probe frequency for measurement and use the same qualified model and low-frequency gain for candidate calculations.
learning.validation: Require analytical and fitted magnitude and phase agreement, retain every crossover, and perturb damping and natural frequency before accepting the candidate for further simulation.
learning.explanation: Inertia and stiffness cancel near the flexible mode, leaving weak damping; shaping adds nominal damping but exact cancellation is model-dependent.
learning.transfer: Bode margins do not by themselves count unstable poles or encirclements; Lesson 48 introduces Nyquist analysis.
